summary: A 1964 two-story concrete and frame lookout on BLM land in Owyhee County, staffed in fire season; the access road crosses mostly private land.

facts.design: Two-story concrete base with a frame cabin (1964 structure)

access.note: Road to the summit is almost all on private land with no recorded BLM right-of-way; signed open to the public as of July 2017 per a climbing guide, and owners could close it. The lookout is a staffed BLM station.

visit.trail_note: Drive-up on a rough road; the final stretch needs 4WD. The climbing guide recommends parking about 3/4 mile short of the summit and walking the rest.

facts.agency: Department of the Interior, Bureau of Land Management (Boise District)

events.note: First lookout on the summit was a cabin; Idaho Fire Lookouts dates it to 1932
Current structure replaced the cabin; described as a two-story concrete base with a frame cabin, or a concrete building with an observation room on top
Burt and Maxine Search listed as known lookout staff
Cloudburst damaged a six-mile stretch of the road used to reach the BLM lookout; reopening estimated at about a week

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Idaho Fire Lookouts gives the first cabin as 1932. Firelookout.com, the NHLR and Forest Lookouts Idaho give 1933. The story uses 1933 for the cabin and notes the 1932 date.

notes_for_editor: Design is described two ways: two-story concrete base with a frame cabin (firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts) versus a concrete building with an observation room (Forest Lookouts Idaho). Both are noted in the story; not resolved. Access evidence is from a climbing guide dated as of July 2017; no current road status found. Staffing is undated. No notable fires found in the sources read, so no fire events are recorded. A BLM Owyhee Field Office closure notice dated 2026-09-19 appeared in search results (blm.gov/sites/default/files/docs/2026-09/20260919_OwyheeFieldOfficeClosure.pdf); it was not read and may not concern South Mountain, so check before adding any fire event. The record's height_m is absent because no source gives a total height.
